title: Lisa and the Little Smudge in the Sky
synopsis: At a dark hillside lookout, Lisa finds a faint fuzzy patch through Grandpa’s binoculars and learns it is a galaxy full of stars.

related_resources.reason: Under sufficiently dark skies Andromeda appears as a faint hazy patch, including through binoculars, and is about 2.5 million light-years away.
The repeated close look and quiet ending invite optional conversation but do not establish any specific benefit of this story.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: “That little smudge is a galaxy,” Grandpa said. “A great gathering of stars, much farther away than the stars we usually see.”
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Under sufficiently dark skies Andromeda appears as a faint hazy patch, including through binoculars, and is about 2.5 million light-years away.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: The science source supports only the natural or physical phenomenon mentioned in the anchor. The characters, plots and observed details of the invented scene are fiction; no impact on sleep, curiosity or learning is established.
